title: The acoustic characteristics of Swedish vowels / SwehVd
why_promising: Primary controlled h-VOWEL-d production from 44 L1 Swedish talkers. The Phonetica study reports that Montreal Forced Aligner word/segment boundaries were manually corrected by the author; F1-F3 were extracted at 20, 35, 50, 65, and 80 percent of each vowel, retaining dynamic trajectories rather than midpoint-only values, and formant outliers were checked. The paper explicitly identifies the public SwehVd OSF repository and a separate public analysis/code OSF project.
open_question: Enumerate the OSF ruxnb file tree and identify downloadable token-level acoustic tables, corrected boundaries/TextGrids, speaker metadata, recordings, units, missing-value conventions, and licensing. If the public tables are derived from the manually corrected boundaries, ingest all five F1-F3 timepoints plus durations and preserve raw Hertz separately from any normalized values.
